component: Orchestration architecture: how the blocks connect (gateway ↔ pipeline ↔ browser), the sync/pacing engine, barge-in and turn-state machine, tool-call race handling, and the transport decision
recommendation: Re-implement VoxEMW's two-process split, but modernize both ends. Pipeline: `pip install "speech-to-speech==1.0.0"` (released 2026-09-06) launched as a SUBPROCESS via its own `serve` CLI on ws://127.0.0.1:8765/v1/realtime — do NOT copy VoxEMW's in-process `launch.py`, which re-implements upstream's startup flow and monkeypatches its internals. Gateway: a ~600-line aiohttp orchestrator on :8000 modelled on voxemw/gateway/orchestrator.py, keeping session-slot retry, persona injection via session.update, speech_started barge-in, heard-prefix write-back, ghost-turn suppression, and the `_resp_active` guard before every response.create — but with WEBSOCKET downlink only (binary PCM16 frames), NO aiortc, NO AudioPacer, NO avatar renderer, audio_lead = 0. Add one thing VoxEMW lacks: a client→server playback-progress event (`{type:"vox.played", ms}` every ~250ms from the WebAudio scheduler) so the server keeps the played-vs-generated distinction that heard-prefix needs without needing a server-side pacer. Frontend: keep his AudioWorklet 16k capture + wsPlayer absolute-timeline WebAudio queue verbatim — that part is already correct.
why:
THE ARCHITECTURE, BLOCK BY BLOCK

Three processes, two hops:
  browser (AudioWorklet mic 16k up / WebAudio queue down)
    ↕ ws://localhost:8000/ws  — OpenAI Realtime events relayed verbatim + a few vox.* control frames
  orchestrator (aiohttp :8000) — ALL product policy lives here
    ↕ ws://127.0.0.1:8765/v1/realtime  — OpenAI Realtime GA event set
  s2s pipeline (:8765) — VAD → STT → LLM → TTS, single session slot, slow to warm

Why the split is right and worth copying: the pipeline is heavy (multi-GB weights, 3-4 min warmup on his 4090, ~1 min even on Mac), single-session, and third-party. The orchestrator is light and restarts in a second. Every piece of behaviour you will iterate on for a debate partner — persona, stance switching, interruption policy, tool calls, echo suppression, scoring — lives in the restartable process. He also proved the seam holds across a total backend swap: the same orchestrator ran Mac/MPS/Qwen3-TTS and 4090/CUDA/VoxCPM2 with only a YAML change. Keep the split; it costs one localhost hop (~1-3ms) each way.

Persona injection (orchestrator.py:69-99, 343-347): browser sends {"type":"vox.persona","id":...}; orchestrator sends session.update with instructions = the persona markdown body, audio.output.voice = persona id, audio.input.turn_detection = {type:"server_vad", interrupt_response:true}. Persona text NEVER enters the pipeline process — so it is hot-swappable mid-session with one message. For a debate partner this is exactly the hook for "switch side / raise difficulty / change accent".

Session slot + connect retry (orchestrator.py:253-281) — copy this verbatim: the pipeline has ONE session slot. After the previous session disconnects, SESSION_END is not released until the handler chain drains, which can take ~10s if TTS was mid-generation. A new connection in that window is accepted and then instantly rejected (session_limit_reached + close 1008). The user-visible symptom is "the first click after a refresh never connects". Fix: connect, wait ≤3s for the first frame, require type=="session.created"; anything else means the slot is still draining → close, sleep 1.5s, retry (6 attempts). Complementary fix (ws_handler:736-739): a new browser connection PREEMPTS the old session (old.close()), so a zombie session from a network change cannot lock you out — no timeout wait, no double refresh.

Barge-in (orchestrator.py:569-607): driven by the upstream `input_audio_buffer.speech_started` event, not by client-side VAD. Three actions fire together — flush the server audio queue, flush the client WebAudio queue, and (the clever part) write the heard prefix back into context.

HEARD-PREFIX WRITE-BACK (orchestrator.py:129-147, 573-586) — the single most transferable idea after the pacer. When the user interrupts, upstream rolls the entire assistant turn out of conversation context. But the user DID hear the first N seconds. Without repair the model has no idea what it already said and repeats itself. Fix: estimate heard text as transcript[: len(transcript) * played_seconds / generated_seconds], back off to the last punctuation so a half-word does not land in context, and if ≥2 chars inject it as an assistant message via conversation.item.create. This requires TWO counters that must not be confused: `_reply_audio_samples` (generated) and pacer.reply_played_seconds (actually played). The played counter MUST be measured at the playback end — TTS runs at RTF 0.4-0.6, so feed position runs far ahead of playback and would wildly overestimate what was heard. He measured generation finishing at 24.7s while playback finished at 51.0s on the same reply. For a debate partner this matters more than for a companion bot: re-arguing a point you already made is the most obvious failure tell.

THE response.create RACES he fixed (all in commit 2e6ce30, all real production bugs):
 (1) Tool turn misjudged as an empty reply. He has an "empty reply fallback": if response.done arrives with no text and no audio, nudge the model to answer again (LLM occasionally emits one token and produces silence). A pure tool-call turn legitimately produces neither → it got nudged and derailed. Fix: `_resp_had_tool_call` set on response.function_call_arguments.done exempts the turn. Plus `_empty_nudged`, a one-shot latch so the nudge cannot loop forever.
 (2) Tool result colliding with an in-flight response. After sending function_call_output you must send response.create for the model to speak. But the tool ran async (VLM took hundreds of ms); if the user barged in meanwhile, upstream ALREADY opened a new response whose context includes the tool output, and response.create is rejected with conversation_already_has_active_response. Fix: track `_resp_active` (set on response.created, cleared on response.done) and skip response.create when a response is already live (orchestrator.py:373-378).
 GENERALIZATION for us: every asynchronous side-channel that terminates in response.create must first check whether a response is already active. Our debate-partner equivalents: a fact-check/retrieval tool, an "assess my argument" tool, a scripted-rebuttal timer.
 (3) `_vision_busy` re-entrancy guard so a second tool call while one is in flight is dropped, not queued.
 (4) Ghost-turn suppression sends response.cancel and then drops every response.* event until response.done or a genuine new speech_started (orchestrator.py:496-500).

GHOST TURNS — two independent, pure, unit-tested filters (orchestrator.py:153-196):
 is_echo: the assistant's own voice leaks from the speakers into the mic and is transcribed as user speech. Rule: normalize away punctuation/whitespace; candidate ≥4 chars; require a ≥4-char CONTIGUOUS match block against one of the last 2 assistant replies AND ≥50% total coverage. The contiguity requirement is the hard-won half — echo replays contiguous audio so it always yields one long contiguous block, whereas a genuine short answer only hits scattered fragments ("我吃了" vs "你吃了吗" = 2-3 chars). He shipped a coverage-only version first and it killed three real user answers in one session (comments dated 2026-08-23). Known accepted false positive: a user deliberately parroting the bot gets muted.
 is_vocabulary_recitation: STT hotword priors hallucinate noise into a recitation of the whole hotword list. Rule: strip hotwords longest-first; ≥2 hits and ZERO residue ⇒ recitation. A single hotword, or any residue, passes.
 FOR ENGLISH these need retuning: his ≥4 "chars" is a CJK assumption. Use ≥4 words (or ≥12 chars) for the contiguous block and case-fold. He also removed the "wear headphones" hint after verifying browser AEC (commit 027f0ff) and STILL needed this text-level filter — so plan on both AEC and echo suppression, not either.

PLAYBACK-DONE ≠ RESPONSE-DONE (orchestrator.py:241-251, 549-554): because TTS generates several times faster than realtime, response.done fires long before the user has heard the reply. Any "is she still speaking" UI state and any turn-taking logic must key on PLAYBACK. Server side he polls pacer.buffered_audio_seconds ≤ 0.02 every 100ms with a 90s cap, then sends vox.playback_done. In WS mode there is no server pacer, so the client falls back to its own remainingMs() timer and the server's signal is explicitly ignored (assistant.js). That is the one genuine hole in his WS design — close it with a client→server playback-progress event.

TWO SMALL ORCHESTRATION WINS worth copying: (a) server-side RMS audio level attached as `lvl` on the relayed audio event, because client-side WebAudio analysers proved unreliable across RTC reconnects / autoplay suspension / WebKit quirks; (b) a no-cache middleware on / and /static, because a stale cached JS produces SILENT audio failure rather than an error. Also: stage-direction stripping ((laughs), *sighs*) must run at SENTENCE level, not delta level — a paren pair gets split across tokens (launch.py:98-106).

=====================================================================
2. THE PACING BUG AND THE DEADLINE-SCHEDULE FIX — the most valuable engineering lesson in the repo
=====================================================================

THE BUG (per-chunk sleep). Original loop:
    while True:
        pcm = await queue.get()
        await ws.send(pcm)
        await asyncio.sleep(len(pcm)/2/16000)   # sleep for the chunk's own duration
Each iteration's real elapsed time is send_time + sleep_time + event-loop scheduling overhead + wakeup latency. asyncio.sleep(d) guarantees AT LEAST d, never exactly d; the error ε is strictly non-negative, so errors accumulate and never cancel. Over N chunks the stream is emitted N·ε late against wall clock. He measured ε/d ≈ 1.2%/minute for the asyncio audio feed and ≈1.6%/minute for the frame drip thread (nominal 25fps actually ran at 24.6fps — the comment in soulx_server.py states this explicitly).

WHY IT IS INVISIBLE SHORT-TERM AND FATAL LONG-TERM: at 5s of speech the video is 60-80ms behind — imperceptible. At 60s it is 0.7-1.0s per stage. The two stages are in series (feed late, then drip late), so cumulative error on the video content axis is ≈2.8%/min ≈ 1.7s per minute of continuous speech (my arithmetic on his two measured rates). Meanwhile the browser plays audio on the sound card's own crystal via sample-exact WebAudio scheduling, so audio NEVER drifts. Result: a monotonically growing lip-sync error, worst at the end of the longest replies — exactly where a user notices. Commit message: "长回复末尾口型可见落后" (visibly lagging lips by the end of long replies).

THE FIX (deadline / absolute timetable). orchestrator.py:384-430 and soulx_server.py:_emit_loop:
    next_t = None
    while True:
        pcm = await queue.get()
        now = time.monotonic()
        if next_t is None: next_t = now
        dur = len(pcm)/2/16000                  # EXACT content duration from sample count
        if now < next_t:
            await asyncio.sleep(next_t - now)   # sleep TO a deadline, not FOR a duration
        await ws.send(pcm)
        next_t += dur                           # advance the VIRTUAL clock by content duration
The invariant: next_t is advanced by content duration computed from sample counts, NEVER from measured wall time. If an iteration overshoots (loop jitter, GC, a slow send), the next iteration finds now ≥ next_t, skips the sleep, sends immediately, and the schedule catches up. Error is bounded by one chunk instead of accumulating. The frame drip thread uses the identical idiom with next_t += 1/fps and threading.Event.wait(next_t - now).

THE THIRD-ORDER TRAP (follow-up fix, commit d2c5049 — 8 hours later, found in real multi-turn use): an absolute timetable is only valid while the stream is CONTINUOUS. After a reply ends the queue idles for seconds and next_t is now far in the past; when the next reply's audio arrives, now ≥ next_t for many consecutive chunks, so the loop dumps the whole new reply as fast as the queue can produce it — a burst that overruns the renderer's bounded queue, drops chunks, and makes the mouth jump. Fix: if the gap since the last send > 0.1s, re-anchor next_t = now. RULE TO CARRY: re-anchor the deadline schedule at every real gap.

FOURTH ORDER: do not confuse a gap with jitter. He keeps a 0.25s jitter tolerance for the stream-break log, and a comment in soulx_server.py warns that shrinking the renderer's own queue.get(timeout=0.2) silence-padding granularity to 0.05s makes normal event-loop feed jitter look like a stream break, padding silence into the middle of speech and destroying lip-sync.

WHAT ALREADY GOT IT RIGHT: rtc.py's audio track used the deadline pattern from day one — `delay = self._start + self._pts/48000 - time.monotonic()`, with pts advancing by exactly 960 samples per 20ms tick. That is the same invariant, which is why the RTC path never drifted; the bug only ever lived in the two hand-rolled loops. And the frontend wsPlayer does it correctly too: `t = max(base, this.nextStart); nextStart = t + buf.duration` — an absolute AudioContext-timeline schedule, not setTimeout. Copy both.

APPLICABILITY TO US: if we drop the renderer there is no second media stream to sync, so no pacing is required and audio should flow to the browser the instant TTS produces it. But the idiom still governs anything we do schedule: an amplitude/viseme visualizer, any rate-limited relay, any "speak this at natural pace" feature, and the client-side WebAudio queue. Extract it as a testable pure function next_deadline(prev, chunk_dur, now, gap_threshold) -> (sleep_for, new_deadline) and unit-test the no-drift and re-anchor properties on a synthetic clock — see §6 for why.

3. WS vs WebRTC FOR OUR LOCALHOST-ONLY MAC — verdict: WebSocket
=====================================================================
His Mac config sets rtc.enabled: true (loopback host candidates work, no TURN needed) and his 4090 config sets false (AutoDL maps TCP only; WebRTC's UDP media has no path, ICE parks in "checking" forever). For our purely local Mac, WS wins anyway:

For WS: (a) drops aiortc + PyAV entirely — a heavy native dependency chain on arm64 that pulls in ffmpeg libs; (b) on loopback TCP there is zero packet loss and ~zero latency, and WebRTC's jitter buffer ADDS 20-60ms of deliberate buffering plus 20ms pacer tick quantization; (c) it removes an entire class of audio-quality bug — aiortc hardcodes Opus application="voip", whose SILK bias smears transients and makes the first phoneme of every reply audibly muffled; he had to monkeypatch OpusEncoder.__init__ to fix it (rtc.py:23-37); (d) 16k→48k resample → Opus encode → decode → resample is pure loss and pure work for zero benefit on loopback; (e) WS is his more recently hardened path (the whole 4090 build runs on it) and the frontend wsPlayer already handles seamless queueing and local flush-on-barge-in; (f) no ICE, no SDP, no trickle workaround, no Safari m-section quirk, no hidden-<audio> Chrome decode workaround.

For WebRTC there is exactly one honest argument — a paced RTP stream with a jitter buffer means the client cannot be overrun. On loopback with a WebAudio queue that is a non-issue, and unpaced delivery is strictly BETTER for latency: the audio is already in the browser before it needs to play.

Not an argument: echo cancellation. getUserMedia({echoCancellation:true}) gives you the browser's AEC on the capture side regardless of downlink transport, and he relied on browser AEC in both modes while still needing the server-side is_echo filter.

Cost of choosing WS: you lose the server-side pacer, hence server knowledge of playback position — needed by vox.playback_done and by heard-prefix. Close it with the client playback-progress event described above. Net: WS + client progress reporting is strictly better than his RTC design for our deployment.

Change to his protocol worth making: he base64s PCM inside the relayed JSON event (33% overhead) purely because he forwards the upstream Realtime event verbatim. On loopback that is irrelevant in bandwidth but wasteful in CPU (json.dumps over a base64 blob per chunk). Send audio as BINARY WS frames on a side channel and keep JSON for control/transcript only. His code already handles binary frames in the browser (they were avatar JPEGs) — the plumbing exists.

4. PIPELINE FOUNDATION: is huggingface/speech-to-speech still right in 2026?
=====================================================================
Yes as a component, no as an integration style.

Upstream status: NOT dead. v1.0.0 shipped 2026-09-06 (three days ago), 13.1k stars, 1,075 commits, PRs merging through early September 2026, "production-tested, powers thousands of Reachy Mini robots". v1.0.0 is BREAKING relative to the 0.2.x/main-@SHA world VoxEMW pins: `--mode realtime`/`--mode local` are replaced by explicit `serve`/`talk`/`local` commands; the `socket` and `raw-websocket` transports are removed; the Realtime engine is now the single unified transport with BOTH WebSocket and WebRTC for the OpenAI Realtime GA event set. It ships Qwen3-ASR, Parakeet TDT, Whisper/Faster-Whisper/MLX Whisper, Paraformer for STT; transformers/MLX/OpenAI-compatible for LLM; Qwen3-TTS, Kokoro, Pocket TTS, ChatTTS, OmniVoice, MMS for TTS; a `--mac-optimal-settings` preset; and Apple-Silicon defaults of mlx-community/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-4bit + 6-bit Qwen3-TTS.

DO NOT COPY HIS INTEGRATION STYLE. voxemw/pipeline/launch.py re-implements upstream's serve flow in-process (parse_arguments → setup_logger → prepare_all_args → build_pipeline → start/wait) and monkeypatches upstream internals (flex_attention compat, torch.hub offline fallback, SmartTurnAnalyzer.__init__). That coupling is why he had to pin a git SHA per deployment (9f59bc72 for Mac, main @3986f5 for 4090) and then write docs/upgrade-regression.md — an entire five-phase runbook — just to change versions. With a real 1.0.0 the correct integration is: pip install speech-to-speech==1.0.0, run its `serve` CLI as a subprocess, talk to it ONLY over the documented Realtime WebSocket. Zero in-process coupling, zero monkeypatches. His custom-backend registration (BackendSpec / STT_BACKENDS / TTS_BACKENDS) is only needed if we ship our own handler; in 2026 upstream likely already has everything we need, so we probably delete backends.py entirely.

vs Pipecat: Pipecat hit v1.0 in April 2026, has near-daily development and the largest vendor-integration library. kwindla/macos-local-voice-agents demonstrates an all-local macOS Pipecat agent at <800ms voice-to-voice on M-series (MLX Whisper + Gemma3n-4B via a local OpenAI-compatible server + Kokoro TTS), with Silero VAD + smart-turn v2 and first-class interruption. That is a published number well inside our 2.0s budget on our hardware class.

Decision framing for an orchestration owner: the OpenAI Realtime GA event set is the STABLE SEAM. Everything valuable in VoxEMW's orchestrator — session.update persona injection, speech_started barge-in, function_call_output tool loop, response.cancel, response.created/done lifecycle — is expressed in that protocol, so it survives a pipeline swap. Pick s2s 1.0.0 as the pipeline because it hands you that protocol for free; keep it behind its own process so swapping to Pipecat (or to a hosted realtime API) later means writing ONE adapter, not rewriting the gateway and the browser. Prototype Pipecat in parallel as the latency fallback; the orchestrator survives either way. (Model-by-model selection is another agent's call; this is purely the integration-seam argument.)

5. FRONTEND (web/assistant.js, 909 lines) — what to keep
=====================================================================
KEEP: AudioWorklet capture at a 16000-rate AudioContext, posting Float32 → Int16 → base64 per callback (no ScriptProcessor). Node connected through a gain=0 node to destination purely to keep the graph pulling. Server-provided `lvl` driving the visualizer instead of a client analyser. wsPlayer's absolute-timeline scheduling (t = max(now+0.03, nextStart); nextStart = t + buf.duration; sources tracked in a Set for batch stop()) — this is the deadline pattern on the client and it is already correct. Barge-in handled locally on input_audio_buffer.speech_started (wsPlayer.flush() stops every scheduled source and resets nextStart) so the client stops instantly without waiting for a server round trip. _needLead reset on both flush and response.done. AudioContext + <audio>.play() warmed inside the mic-button click handler because autoplay policy requires a gesture. visibilitychange handler that re-checks ws / RTC / mic on foreground. Mic track onended/onmute handlers with a 3s self-heal window — iOS/WKWebView suspends the audio session between playbacks, the mic track goes muted/ended, the page looks fine and uplink audio silently stops ("it just stops talking after a few turns"); this was diagnosed from logs showing the pipeline re-enabled listening and then received nothing. 3s auto-reconnect on ws close, but only if the mic is live (otherwise two devices ping-pong preempting each other forever).

DROP: everything WebRTC (startRTC's 15s ICE-gathering wait for aiortc's lack of trickle; the relay-vs-all iceTransportPolicy heuristic; the hidden <audio> element that exists only because Chrome will not decode a remote RTC track routed straight into WebAudio; the Safari addTransceiver workaround; the /rtc/debug telemetry). The avatar canvas and JPEG blob path. The 1.5s camera-frame upload loop unless we want vision. The starfield canvas is decoration — but note the state machine driving it (idle / listening / thinking / speaking, with thinking entered on speech_stopped and speaking entered on the first audio delta) is a clean, correct turn-state model worth keeping in whatever UI we build.

6. TESTS — where the bugs actually were, read positively AND negatively
=====================================================================
tests/ is 6 files, ~570 lines, ALL pure-function: zero models, zero network, zero GPU, runs in a bare venv with pytest+pyyaml+numpy+aiohttp. Every tricky piece of logic was deliberately factored into a module-level pure function so it could be tested — the docstrings literally say 便于单测 ("easy to unit test"). That is the shape to copy.
 - test_audio_pacer.py (96): tick exactness and silence padding, lead hold-then-play, lead applied only on empty→non-empty transitions, flush resets counters, reply_played_seconds tracks the CURRENT reply across reply boundaries, fade-in curve shape (first sample 0, midpoint proportional, past the window untouched, empty/short input safe). Timing behaviour is tested by driving a fake consumer (call next_audio_tick N times) rather than sleeping — which is possible only because the pacer is a pure state machine over a monotonic clock.
 - test_orchestrator.py (142): heard_prefix proportional cut + punctuation backoff + every return-empty boundary; session.update shape incl. tools; parse_function_call_done incl. missing fields; event classification for BOTH the GA and beta audio-delta event names (response.output_audio.delta / response.audio.delta) — protocol-drift insurance; and 8 assertions on is_echo / is_vocabulary_recitation, several literally labelled with the date of the false-positive incident that motivated them.
 - test_config.py (194, the largest): config validation and sys.exit behaviour. Cheap, and it catches the "started, then died three minutes into model loading" class.
 - test_pipeline_args.py (160): argv rendering. test_launch.py (22): stage-direction stripping. test_vision.py (56): VLM client with httpx faked into sys.modules.
THE NEGATIVE SPACE IS THE REAL LESSON: there are NO tests for the paced feed loop, the frame drip loop, or the RTC track — and that is precisely where the 1.2%/1.6% drift lived for weeks and where the re-anchoring bug then appeared. Those loops were left untested because they "need real time". Do not repeat that: extract the schedule as a pure function over an injected clock and test drift-free advance, catch-up after an overshoot, and re-anchor after a gap.

7. audio_lead_ms: 1300 — what it is, and why it disappears for us
=====================================================================
The talking-head renderer has a fixed STRUCTURAL latency: it consumes audio in 0.96s chunks (24 frames @25fps) and takes ~0.25s to generate each chunk, so the video for a given instant of audio appears ≈1.21s after that audio was fed. Because the whole chain runs on ONE clock (audio is fed to the renderer at PLAYBACK rate, and the renderer drips frames at 25fps), the video stream is simply a constant ~1.2s behind the audio stream — no timestamps needed anywhere. Rather than build explicit sync, he delays the AUDIO by the same amount. 1300 not 1210 because he needed headroom for the model's inherent ~0.5s "opening the mouth from idle" transition, worst-case TTS jitter, and the vision tool stealing GPU.
Two implementations of one idea: in WS mode the frontend delays only the FIRST chunk of each reply by leadSec (wsPlayer._needLead), with subsequent chunks queueing seamlessly behind it and the flag reset on flush and response.done; in RTC mode the server-side AudioPacer sets _audio_ready_at = monotonic() + lead on the queue's empty→non-empty transition and emits silence until then, exposed as ?alead= for debugging.
THE COST IS A DIRECT 1.3s ADDITION TO PERCEIVED LATENCY. His final number was ~3.2s to first sound = 1.9s thinking chain + 1.3s lead. He then spent a full day trying to buy that back with explicit timestamp sync (feed at generation speed, 4-byte timestamp per frame, client-side cursor scheduling), fixed ~10 bugs (zeroing race, silent half-chunk contamination, negative timestamps, seam stalls, a cursor sign error), and ended up back at 1.35s — the physical constraints do not move with architecture. He rolled the whole thing back (commit 6212d71) and recorded the decision.
FOR US THIS IS DECISIVE: our target is <2.0s with a 3.0s ceiling. The lead alone eats 1.3s. DO NOT SHIP A DIFFUSION TALKING HEAD. Dropping the renderer sets audio_lead = 0 and deletes the AudioPacer, the avatar feed pacer, the frame relay, the reconnect logic, and the entire class of sync bugs. What survives is the deadline idiom, the played-vs-fed distinction, and playback_done.
If a face is wanted later, the only lead-free options are ones whose visual latency is ~0: a 2D/3D rig driven by visemes or amplitude (his own v1.9.0 did exactly this — VRM + a wLipSync reimplementation, with viseme frames pushed through the SAME pacer as the audio so they popped at the same instant, lead 0), or a pure waveform/orb visualizer. Same single-clock principle, zero lead.

8. ENVIRONMENT TRAPS — every one the author recorded
=====================================================================
NETWORK / PROXY
 1. no_proxy for localhost websockets (start_mac.sh:23-26). With a global http_proxy set, the `websockets` library routes the orchestrator→pipeline ws://127.0.0.1:8765 handshake THROUGH the proxy and the handshake dies with EOF. export no_proxy="127.0.0.1,localhost,::1" AND NO_PROXY (both cases). We will hit this — websockets, httpx and aiohttp all honour proxy env vars.
 2. socksio (mac_setup.sh:44-46). With SOCKS proxy env vars set, huggingface_hub's httpx raises ImportError on download. pip install "httpx[socks]".
 3. HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 at runtime once weights are cached (start_mac.sh:20-21) — otherwise every start hits the network. Caveat: the FIRST Silero VAD load still needs network because it goes through torch.hub.
 4. HF download flakiness: HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET=1 needed on some networks; direct huggingface.co beat hf-mirror on his network (hf-mirror returned "Local entry not found" while direct downloaded instantly); HF_ENDPOINT is the override knob (mac_setup.sh:29-31).
DEPENDENCY PINS
 5. torchcodec uninstalled defensively — conflicts with transformers 5.x (mac_setup.sh:48-49).
 6. transformers ↔ torch skew: transformers 5.13's flex_attention integration top-level-imports torch.nn.attention.flex_attention.AuxRequest, which exists only in torch ≥2.9; on torch 2.8 the entire import chain dies even though flex attention is never used. He injects a placeholder class (launch.py:30-42). Pin torch and transformers TOGETHER.
 7. transformers 5.16.1 MiniCPM-V-4.6 slicing regression — vectorized window merge crashes on non-uniform slices; he ran the VLM in a separate env pinned to transformers==5.7.0 to restore the 36-slice OCR quality (vlm_server.py:3-6).
 8. transformers 5.16 continue_final_message=True is incompatible with the Qwen3-ASR chat template (renders without the last message → ValueError); hand-assemble the assistant prefill string instead (stt_qwen3asr.py:95).
 9. torch.hub offline fallback (launch.py:45-66): Silero VAD calls torch.hub.load("snakers4/silero-vad") on EVERY startup and fails when GitHub is flaky. He wraps torch.hub.load to retry with source="local" from torch.hub.get_dir()/snakers4_silero-vad_master. Better fix for us: use an ONNX Silero so torch.hub never runs.
MODEL-LOADING LANDMINES
 10. Qwen3-ASR MUST use the -hf variant. The non-hf repo uses thinker.* key layout; transformers' qwen3_asr expects model.audio_tower.*. Loading does NOT error — audio_tower/projector are silently randomly initialized and you only find out at forward time with "Audio features and audio tokens do not match, tokens: 13, features: 13" (counts equal, dims not). Generalize: after loading any model, assert no missing keys.
 11. MLX quantization is NOT monotonic in quality: Qwen3-TTS at bf16 doubled TTFA (0.5→1.1s) and generation could no longer keep up with playback because of 2.6x memory bandwidth — he stayed at 6-bit. DIRECTLY RELEVANT TO OUR 128GB BOX: more RAM does not fix a bandwidth-bound TTS. Bigger quant ≠ better.
 12. Pipeline sample rate is 16kHz end to end and the config says 勿改 (do not change). Any 24k/48k TTS is resampled inside its handler.
 13. STT hotwords are a hallucination hazard: 10 hotwords made the model hallucinate the entire wordlist out of pure noise; he cut to 2-3 and added deterministic post-correction (assistant.yaml:29-34).
 14. Reasoning-by-default models must have thinking disabled: DeepSeek v4-flash thinks ~2s before the first token unless reasoning_effort:"none" (assistant.yaml:48).
UPSTREAM API COUPLING
 15. Registration order: register_custom_backends() must run BEFORE `import speech_to_speech.s2s_pipeline`, because ModuleArguments' stt/tts choices are frozen at import time (launch.py:140-147).
 16. BackendSpec.config_type must be a DISTINCT dataclass per backend — reusing one triggers argparse option-string conflicts (backends.py:19-29).
 17. A custom TTS factory must pass should_listen from HandlerContext; built-in backends get it via setup_args (backends.py:69-72).
 18. Never copy a venv — shebangs hardcode the path. Build a fresh one (upgrade-regression.md:20).
WEBRTC / BROWSER (moot if we go WS, kept for completeness)
 19. aiortc hardcodes Opus application="voip" → SILK smears transients → first phoneme muffled. Monkeypatch OpusEncoder.__init__ to set codec.options={"application":"audio"} (rtc.py:23-37).
 20. aiortc has no trickle ICE — the browser must gather ALL candidates before POSTing the offer (he waits up to 15s on icegatheringstatechange).
 21. Chrome only decodes a remote WebRTC audio track when it is attached to a media element; routing it straight into WebAudio is silent on Chrome (works on Safari; MediaRecorder appears to work because recording forces decode).
 22. Safari: createOffer({offerToReceive*}) yields a zero-m-section offer (server 500); use addTransceiver("audio",{direction:"recvonly"}).
 23. Mixing a public TURN with a loopback peer always fails — Cloudflare refuses CHANNEL_BIND toward 127.0.0.1 (SSRF protection). Both sides must use identical ICE config. And forcing iceTransportPolicy:"relay" on a pure-localhost setup yields zero candidates and a dead connection, which is why his frontend forces relay only when the server actually handed down TURN servers.
 24. iOS getUserMedia requires https — hence the optional LAN TLS listener on :9443. localhost is a secure context, so plain http is fine on the Mac itself.
 25. Autoplay policy: AudioContext starts suspended and <audio>.play() needs a user gesture; warm both inside the mic-button click handler.
 26. iOS/WKWebView suspends the audio session between playbacks and mutes/ends the mic track silently (see §5).
OPS
 27. pkill -f self-suicide: the pattern must not appear in your own command line — use the bracket trick 'voxemw.pipeline.launc[h]' and keep kill and start in separate shell invocations (start_4090.sh:12).
 28. set -u breaks some conda activate.d scripts (start_4090.sh:5).
 29. FastAPI + `from __future__ import annotations`: stringified annotations mean a type imported INSIDE the function body cannot be resolved, and FastAPI silently downgrades the body param to a query param → 422 "query req Field required". Web-framework-related imports must be module level (vlm_server.py, plan-4090.md:149-152).
 30. Disk: 108GB filled from duplicate HF + ModelScope + pip caches. nltk punkt_tab BadZipFile from an interrupted download — delete the directory and refetch.

evidence.claim: The per-chunk-sleep pacing bug accumulated measured drift of 1.2% (audio feed) and 1.6% (frame drip) per minute, visibly lagging lip-sync by the end of long replies; both were fixed by switching to deadline-schedule dispatch
evidence.detail: Commit message: '音画同步：paced 喂入与帧滴灌的 per-chunk sleep 误差累积（实测 1.2%/1.6% 每分钟）→ 双 deadline 时刻表调度，长回复零漂移'. The diff replaces `await asyncio.sleep(len(pcm)/2/16000)` with a virtual timetable `next_t` advanced by exact content duration, sleeping only `next_t - now`. soulx_server.py's _emit_loop diff replaces `target = time.perf_counter() + frame_interval` per frame with `next_t += frame_interval`, and its new docstring states the measured consequence: '后者每帧都多吃一点调度开销（实测 24.6fps < 25），视频内容轴比实时慢 ~1.6%'.

evidence.claim: An absolute deadline schedule must be re-anchored after any real gap, or the next burst overruns downstream bounded queues
evidence.detail: Follow-up fix 8 hours after the deadline change: '>0.1s 喂入间隙后旧时刻表已过期，新回复音频按旧表「补发」成洪峰，冲爆渲染端有界队列丢音频块 → 嘴型跳乱（11:16/11:21 用户会话实测）'. Adds `if gap > 0.1: next_t = now`, and gates the stream-break log on `self._resp_active` so normal turn-taking gaps are not logged as breaks.

evidence.claim: The RTC audio track already used the deadline pattern from the start, which is why it never drifted — the bug lived only in the two hand-rolled loops
evidence.detail: `delay = self_._start + self_._pts / AUDIO_RATE - time.monotonic(); if delay > 0: await asyncio.sleep(delay)` with `self_._pts += AUDIO_TICK_48K` (960 samples) per tick. Comment: '20ms 实时节奏（超前就睡到点；落后直接发，靠 pts 保对齐）'. Same invariant: pts advances by exact sample count, never by measured wall time.

evidence.claim: audio_lead_ms 1300 is a direct 1.3s addition to perceived latency, exists solely to compensate the diffusion renderer's structural lag, and is unrecoverable by better sync architecture
evidence.detail: Config comment: '渲染链路固有滞后 = 0.96s 攒 chunk + ~0.25s 生成 ≈ 1.21s，声音压后同量即唇形对齐'. docs/plan-4090.md:161-180 records the failed attempt to reduce it: explicit timestamp sync was built to cut 3.2s → 2.6s, cost ~10 bugs in one day, and ended at lead 1.35s ≈ the original 1.3s — '延迟目标没有达成，复杂度全款付清'. Rolled back in commit 6212d71. Final measured: 开口 ~3.2s = 思考链 1.9s + lead 1.3s.

evidence.claim: The s2s pipeline exposes exactly one session slot, and the slot is not released until the handler chain drains (~10s if TTS is mid-generation), causing 'first click never connects'
evidence.detail: _connect_s2s_with_retry: '管线只有 1 个会话槽：上个会话断开后 SESSION_END 要等 handler 链排空才释放（TTS 还在生成时能拖到 ~10s），这期间新连接被 accept 后秒拒（session_limit_reached + 1008）。表现就是「刷新/首点必连不上」'. Liveness probe: first frame must be type=='session.created' within 3s, else close + 1.5s sleep, 6 attempts. Corroborated by docs/plan-4090.md item 9.

evidence.claim: response.create must be guarded by an is-response-active check whenever it follows an async side-channel, and tool turns must be exempted from the empty-reply fallback
evidence.detail: _tool_vision_turn: after sending function_call_output, `if self._resp_active: logger.info('用户已抢话，跳过 response.create'); return`. _resp_active set on response.created (L523-524), cleared on response.done (L545). Separately _resp_had_tool_call (L506) exempts tool turns from the empty-reply nudge at L556-568, which is itself latched by _empty_nudged. Commit 2e6ce30 message names both: '修复 tool 回合被空回复兜底误判、用户抢话与工具回注撞 response.create 两个竞态'. docs/upgrade-regression.md:14 also lists 'response.create 被拒（conversation_already_has_active_response）重试' as a depended-on protocol behaviour.

evidence.claim: Interruption repair requires writing the heard prefix back to context, computed from PLAYED (not fed) audio, because TTS RTF<1 makes fed position wildly overestimate what the user heard
evidence.detail: heard_prefix(transcript, audio_seconds, played_seconds) cuts proportionally then backs off to the last punctuation; <2 chars returns '' (keep the upstream rollback). Applied at L573-586 as a conversation.item.create assistant message. audio_pacer.py:46-49 explains why played is tracked separately: '打断回报估算「用户实际听到了多少」靠它而不是喂入时钟（TTS 生成快于播放 RTF<1，按喂入量算会高估）'.

evidence.claim: Generation-done is not playback-done: measured 24.7s generation vs 51.0s playback on the same reply
evidence.detail: Commit: '生成完毕≠播完（TTS 生成比播放快数倍），orchestrator 监听 pacer 队列清空后下发 vox.playback_done，前端收到才收状态；45s 兜底 + 播放尾段波纹地板。实测：生成 24.7s 完，播放 51.0s 完，信号精准'. Implemented as _notify_playback_done (orchestrator.py:241-251), polling buffered_audio_seconds<=0.02 at 100ms with a 900-iteration (90s) cap.

evidence.claim: Server-side echo suppression is still needed even with browser AEC enabled, and the working rule requires a CONTIGUOUS match block, not just coverage
evidence.detail: is_echo: normalize punctuation, candidate >=4 chars, longest contiguous SequenceMatcher block >=4 AND coverage >=0.5. Docstring: '连续块要求是关键——回声重放的是连续音频，必然带出长连续块；而真实短答只会撞上零散文案（「我吃了」撞「你吃了吗」就 2-3 字），2026-08-23 实测三轮误杀后加这道'. Meanwhile commit 027f0ff removed the 'wear headphones' UI hint with '浏览器 AEC 已验证可靠', and getUserMedia is called with echoCancellation:true — so AEC was on and this filter was still required.

evidence.claim: huggingface/speech-to-speech is actively maintained and shipped a breaking v1.0.0 on 2026-09-06, making VoxEMW's git-SHA pinning strategy obsolete
evidence.detail: v1.0.0 released 2026-09-06: three commands serve/talk/local replace --mode flags; Realtime engine is the single unified transport with BOTH WebSocket and WebRTC over the OpenAI Realtime GA event set; socket and raw-websocket transports removed; Qwen3-ASR STT and OpenAI-compatible STT/TTS endpoints supported; Apple Silicon defaults to mlx-community/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-4bit + 6-bit Qwen3-TTS. evidence.detail: MLX Whisper STT + Gemma3n 4B via an OpenAI-compatible local server + Kokoro TTS (mlx-community/Kokoro-82M-bf16), with Silero VAD and smart-turn v2 for semantic end-of-turn detection; interruption supported. evidence.detail: _patch_opus_quality: 'aiortc 的 Opus 编码器硬编 application=voip：SILK 偏向的语音优化会抹平瞬态——回复开头第一个音发闷/发糊（用户实测可闻）。切 audio 模式（全频 MDCT，瞬态保真）'. evidence.detail: cf114f7: 'v2.2.0：大脑回归 DeepSeek API，摘除本地 LLM（llama.cpp/MiniCPM，16G Mac 质量不达标）'; config comment: '本地 8B 脑实测回复质量不达标'. evidence.claim: The client already implements the correct absolute-timeline scheduling pattern for WebAudio playback, including per-response lead and batch-stop barge-in
evidence.detail: wsPlayer.feed: `const base = firstOfResponse ? ctx.currentTime + 0.03 + this.leadSec : ctx.currentTime + 0.03; const t = Math.max(base, this.nextStart); src.start(t); this.nextStart = t + buf.duration;` with sources tracked in a Set. flush() stops every scheduled source, resets nextStart=0 and _needLead=true. Fired locally from the input_audio_buffer.speech_started handler so the client stops instantly without a server round-trip.

evidence.detail: 6 files, ~570 lines, runnable with only pytest+pyyaml+numpy+aiohttp per README. test_audio_pacer.py drives a fake consumer instead of sleeping; test_orchestrator.py covers heard_prefix, session.update, parse_function_call_done, GA+beta audio event names, and 8 is_echo/is_vocabulary_recitation cases labelled with incident dates. Those are precisely the sites of the 1.2%/1.6% drift and the re-anchoring bug.

evidence.claim: Chrome will not decode a remote WebRTC audio track unless it is attached to a media element, and Safari needs addTransceiver rather than the legacy offerToReceive options
evidence.detail: 'Chrome 对 WebRTC 远端音轨只有挂到媒体元素上才开始解码（WebAudio 直通在 Chrome 里是静音，Safari 正常；MediaRecorder 能录到是因为录制强制解码。2026-08-23 实测定案）'. And at startRTC: '显式 recvonly transceiver：Safari 对 createOffer({offerToReceive*}) 老语法会产出零 m-section 的空 offer（iPad 实测 500）'. Both disappear if the downlink is a WebSocket.

evidence.claim: iOS/WKWebView silently suspends the audio session and mutes the mic track, producing a page that looks alive but stops sending uplink audio
evidence.detail: 'iOS WKWebView 会在播放间隙把音频会话挂起，麦克风轨道被系统 mute/end，页面看起来正常但上行再没声音（聊几轮就「自动不聊」的元凶，2026-08-24 日志实锤：管线 listening re-enabled 后再没收到任何音频）'. Fix: track.onended → restart immediately; track.onmute → 3s self-heal window then restart. Plus a visibilitychange handler that re-checks ws/RTC/mic on foreground.

evidence.claim: The pipeline's 16kHz end-to-end sample rate is a hard invariant, and STT hotwords are a hallucination hazard above ~3 entries
evidence.detail: '热词偏置（概率性，务必克制：词越多模型越容易把没说的话脑补成词表内容——2026-08-23 实测 10 个词时整段幻觉出词表。只留人设核心词 + corrections 兜底）'; commit 05c4c29 cut the list from 10 to 3. Separately tts.sample_rate: 16000 is annotated '管线全程 16kHz，勿改'. The hotword hallucination is what motivated is_vocabulary_recitation.

alternatives.name: Pipecat 1.x as the pipeline instead of speech-to-speech 1.0.0
alternatives.tradeoff: You give up the OpenAI Realtime protocol as a free, standard seam — which is what makes every piece of VoxEMW's orchestrator logic (session.update persona injection, speech_started barge-in, function_call_output tool loop, response.cancel, response lifecycle) portable — and you write the browser protocol yourself or adopt Pipecat's client SDKs. In exchange you get a Python-native pipeline you fully own, the largest integration library, near-daily development, smart-turn v2 semantic end-of-turn, and a published <800ms all-local voice-to-voice number on M-series Macs (kwindla/macos-local-voice-agents).
alternatives.when_to_prefer: If s2s 1.0.0's Mac path cannot hit the <2.0s budget in measurement, or if we need per-stage control the Realtime protocol does not expose (custom interrupt policy inside the pipeline, speculative TTS, per-sentence rewriting). Because the orchestrator sits behind the Realtime seam, switching costs one adapter, not a rewrite — so prototype Pipecat in parallel from day one as the latency fallback.

alternatives.name: Browser talks to the s2s Realtime WebSocket directly, no orchestrator process
alternatives.tradeoff: Saves one localhost hop (~2-6ms, irrelevant) and one process. Costs you every piece of product policy: no persona hot-swap, no heard-prefix write-back on barge-in, no echo/ghost-turn suppression, no tool-call race guarding, no session-slot preemption or connect retry, no server-side audio level, and no place to put debate-specific logic. It also means every policy change requires reloading the model process.
alternatives.when_to_prefer: A throwaway latency-measurement spike in the first day or two, to establish the raw pipeline floor before the orchestrator exists. Never for the actual product.

alternatives.name: WebRTC (aiortc) downlink with the AudioPacer, as his Mac config sets
alternatives.tradeoff: Adds aiortc + PyAV native deps on arm64, ICE/SDP plumbing, the Opus voip→audio monkeypatch, the hidden-<audio> Chrome workaround, the Safari addTransceiver workaround, aiortc's no-trickle 15s gather wait, and 20-60ms of jitter buffer plus 20ms pacer quantization — for zero benefit on loopback. In exchange you get a server-side pacer, which restores authoritative server knowledge of playback position (vox.playback_done, reply_played_seconds for heard-prefix) without a custom client event.
alternatives.when_to_prefer: When the client stops being the same machine — a phone or tablet on LAN or WAN — where a jitter buffer and congestion control genuinely matter. Design the orchestrator so the downlink transport is one swappable module and the playback-position source is an interface with two implementations (server pacer / client report).

alternatives.name: Native macOS or iOS client instead of a browser
alternatives.tradeoff: Loses instant iteration, cross-device access, and the whole WebAudio/AudioWorklet stack that already works. Gains AVAudioSession .voiceChat mode, which is system-level AEC rather than browser AEC, plus reliable background/lock-screen audio — he built exactly this iOS shell in v1.8.1 for those reasons.
alternatives.when_to_prefer: Only if measurement shows browser AEC on macOS leaks enough assistant audio into the mic that the text-level is_echo filter is firing regularly during real debate turns. Test AEC on the browser first with real speakers before spending a day on a native shell.

latency_estimate:
ORCHESTRATION LAYER ONLY (excludes VAD/STT/LLM/TTS, which other agents own).

WebSocket design (recommended): ~25-55ms end to end of added latency.
 - Uplink browser→orchestrator→pipeline: two loopback WS hops. Per-frame JSON+base64 serialize/deserialize on 20-64ms audio frames is single-digit microseconds of CPU; loopback TCP RTT on macOS is ~0.05-0.2ms. Budget 2-5ms total.
 - Downlink pipeline→orchestrator→browser: same two hops, plus one json.dumps over the base64 audio blob when attaching the `lvl` RMS field (his design). A 100ms 16k mono chunk is 3.2KB raw / 4.3KB base64 — sub-millisecond. Sending binary PCM frames on a side channel removes even that. Budget 2-5ms.
 - Client WebAudio scheduling cushion: his wsPlayer adds a fixed +30ms on every chunk (ctx.currentTime + 0.03) to guarantee the source starts in the future. This is the single largest orchestration cost and it is deliberate — shrink it to ~15ms only if you measure no underruns.
 - audio_lead: 0 with no renderer.
 - The extra orchestrator process (browser↔gateway↔pipeline rather than browser↔pipeline) costs one loopback hop each way, i.e. ~1-3ms round trip. That is 0.1% of a 2000ms budget and buys a restartable policy layer. Keep it.

WebRTC design (not recommended here): ~65-125ms, i.e. 40-70ms worse. Adds 16k→48k resample + Opus encode on the server, decode + jitter buffer on the client (20-60ms of deliberate buffering), and the pacer's 20ms tick quantization (up to 20ms of waiting for the next tick boundary even when audio is ready).

WITH A DIFFUSION TALKING HEAD: +1300ms, non-negotiable. His measured end-to-end was ~3.2s to first sound = 1.9s thinking chain + 1.3s lead, and a full day of explicit-sync engineering could not reduce the lead below ~1.35s. That single number decides the renderer question against us: our ceiling is 3.0s and our target is 2.0s.

CONCLUSION: orchestration contributes roughly 1.5-3% of a 2000ms budget in the WS design. The two orchestration decisions that actually move the needle are (a) audio_lead = 0 (no renderer) and (b) letting audio flow to the browser the instant the first TTS chunk exists rather than pacing it — i.e. NOT porting the AudioPacer. Everything else in the gateway is noise against STT/LLM/TTS time.
memory_gb: Orchestration layer only: ~0.15-0.3 GB RSS. An aiohttp + websockets + numpy gateway process is ~100-200MB; adding aiortc + PyAV pushes it to ~300-400MB plus native ffmpeg libs (avoidable by choosing the WS design). Per-session buffers are trivial: his AudioPacer holds a bytearray of undrained TTS audio — at 16k mono PCM16 that is 32KB/s, and a 30s backlog is under 1MB. The avatar feed queue was documented as peaking under 1MB for a 30s reply. On a 128GB machine the gateway is free; the entire memory budget belongs to the model processes. Practical implication: because the gateway is memory-free and restarts in ~1s, put ALL iterating logic in it and never restart the pipeline process to change behaviour.

risks: s2s 1.0.0 is THREE DAYS OLD (released 2026-09-06) and is a breaking release: serve/talk/local commands replace --mode flags, socket and raw-websocket transports are gone, and defaults changed. Every VoxEMW CLI-rendering assumption in voxemw/pipeline/args.py is stale. Budget a day to read `serve --help` and the new quickstart before writing the argv layer, and expect early-1.0 bugs.

The single-session-slot behaviour, the 1008/session_limit_reached rejection, and 'session.created is always the first frame' are UNDOCUMENTED upstream behaviours his retry loop depends on. If 1.0.0 changed any of them the retry logic silently degrades into a 9-second stall on every reconnect. Verify by force-reconnecting twice in a row during TTS generation and reading the actual close code.

Whether `interrupt_response: true` + server_vad still emits input_audio_buffer.speech_started as the barge-in signal in 1.0.0 is unverified. That single event is the trigger for flush + heard-prefix + client stop; if the event name or semantics moved, barge-in silently stops working with no error.

Dropping the server-side pacer means the server no longer knows playback position. His WS mode papers over this with a client-side timer and explicitly ignores the server's vox.playback_done. Our client playback-progress event is a design I am proposing, not one he validated — it needs a clock-skew story (report AudioContext-relative ms deltas, not absolute timestamps) and a stale-report guard after flush.

is_echo's thresholds are CJK character-count based (>=4 chars contiguous, >=50% coverage). Ported verbatim to English they will over-fire: 4 English characters is a fragment of one word. Retune to >=4 words or >=12 characters and case-fold, and unit-test against real transcripts before shipping — his own history shows a mis-tuned version killed three genuine user turns in one session.

Browser AEC on macOS is the unvalidated assumption in the whole design. He ran with echoCancellation:true and STILL needed text-level echo suppression. If AEC leaks badly with laptop speakers at conversational volume, the debate partner will interrupt itself and the fallbacks are (a) headphones, (b) a native shell with AVAudioSession .voiceChat. Test with real speakers on day one, not headphones.

Python 3.12 vs the installed 3.14: uv will download 3.12, which is correct, but any teammate who runs the gateway under 3.14 out of habit will hit missing torch/mlx wheels deep inside the pipeline import chain with a confusing error. Pin the interpreter in the start script and assert it at startup.

A global http_proxy on this machine will break the localhost WebSocket handshake with a bare EOF and no useful message. This is the single most likely 'why does nothing work' failure on first run. Set no_proxy AND NO_PROXY in the launcher, and log the effective values at startup so it is diagnosable in one look.

The deadline-schedule lesson is easy to nod at and then re-introduce. Any future 'stream this at natural pace' feature (paced audio, a viseme track, a typing-effect transcript, rate limiting) written as sleep(duration-per-item) will reproduce the exact 1.2-1.6%/min drift. Encode it once as a shared, unit-tested scheduler helper before anyone needs it a second time.

If anyone later asks for a face, the 1.3s lead comes back with a diffusion renderer and blows the budget on its own. Decide now that any avatar must be viseme- or amplitude-driven with zero structural lag (his own v1.9.0 VRM approach, lead 0), and write that constraint down where the product decision gets made.
open_questions: Does s2s 1.0.0's Realtime GA event set already include a client→server playback-position event? If so, use it instead of inventing vox.played — check the v1.0.0 event reference before writing the custom protocol.

Does 1.0.0's `serve` still enforce one session per pipeline (num_pipelines), and does it still reject a second connection with close 1008 after a session.created-less first frame? This determines whether the retry+preempt logic is still needed or is now dead code.

In 1.0.0, is the barge-in signal still input_audio_buffer.speech_started, and is SmartTurn v3 semantic end-of-turn wired to the same event or a new one? Semantic turn detection is more important for a debate partner than for a companion bot — you must not cut in on a mid-argument pause.

Do we need custom backend registration at all under 1.0.0? Upstream now ships Parakeet TDT, Whisper/MLX Whisper, Qwen3-ASR, Kokoro, Qwen3-TTS and OpenAI-compatible endpoints natively — if so we delete voxemw/pipeline/backends.py, launch.py and args.py entirely and integrate purely via the serve CLI.

Measured: does Chrome's AEC on macOS cancel WebAudio-scheduled playback as reliably as it cancels WebRTC playback? This is the one place where the WS-vs-WebRTC decision could flip, and it is answerable in 20 minutes with real speakers.

What are the right English thresholds for is_echo (contiguous-block length, coverage) against real ASR transcripts of our own TTS voice? Needs a small labelled corpus of genuine short answers vs. captured echo before shipping.

For a debate partner specifically: should barge-in be softened? VoxEMW cuts audio instantly on speech_started. A debate opponent that stops mid-sentence at every 'uh-huh' feels weak; one that talks over you feels rude. Consider a short (~250-400ms) confirmation window before flushing, using the pipeline's own speech_stopped/turn signal — but note the heard-prefix machinery must then account for the extra audio played during that window.

Does the s2s LLM proxy feature (--enable_llm_proxy) let us run debate scoring / argument tracking as a background LLM call without interrupting the live conversation? That would be a cleaner home for it than a tool call, which has to fight the response.create race.

Whether the >0.1s re-anchor threshold and the 0.25s jitter tolerance are the right constants for our machine, if we end up pacing anything at all. They were tuned against his renderer's 0.2s silence-padding granularity, which we will not have.
